extraction.name: MathVista
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts, consisting of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was compiled by collecting 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets, reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and selecting 19 publicly available math-related ones, and creating 3 new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). Existing VQA examples were first heuristically filtered for likely mathematical reasoning and then manually labeled by expert annotators. New datasets were manually annotated and reviewed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 85.6% of examples have annotations because annotations were sourced from original data providers and are heterogeneous.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from 31 source datasets: 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing VQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets. The new datasets were sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic illustrations from online education resources, with PaperQA examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples for balanced representation. The dataset was split into testmini and test, with testmini sampled by first taking up to 4 questions per source dataset and then sampling remaining questions proportionally to the full distribution.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning by choosing examples with numeric answers or quantity words in the questions. This automatic filtration was followed by manual labeling to remove false positives. Several quality checks were also conducted to address unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and mathematical reasoning types. For filtering VQA examples, three expert annotators labeled whether examples involved mathematical reasoning using Yes/No/Unsure options and detailed instructions. The three new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and reviewed in a two-step process by three reviewers, with disagreements resolved by discussion. Mathematical reasoning labels were automatically obtained from source details and verified by expert annotators on 1,000 examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool GUI; Amazon Mechanical Turk for human performance baseline and Bard assessment
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Majority voting was used for VQA mathematical reasoning labels. For the new datasets, three reviewers independently annotated each dataset, achieving 99.2% inter-annotation consistency; 6 disagreements among 736 questions were resolved through team discussion. For mathematical reasoning labeling, automatic and human annotations matched exactly on 94.1% of examples and 98.79% of individual labels. For mathematical-problem labeling, Fleiss' Kappa among three annotators was 0.775.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields; expert annotators; human annotators with a high school diploma or higher; AMT annotators with more than 5,000 HIT tasks completed and acceptance score higher than 0.99
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 answer extractor; EasyOCR; Multimodal Bard for image captions
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Answer labels for the test split will not be publicly released; an online evaluation platform will be maintained. The authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language, grade level, and educational attainment of human annotators
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support development of general-purpose AI agents for mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, including education, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Annotations come from heterogeneous original data providers and lack a unified format and structure; larger numbers of few-shot examples can introduce demonstration bias in LLM evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may have gaps in coverage of certain mathematical problems and visuals; collecting high-quality data is labor-intensive; scalability and generalizability to other domains remain concerns; only 85.6% of examples have annotations; annotations are heterogeneous and not unified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts; testmini is intended for model development validation or limited computing resources, while test is for standard evaluation.
